current_bottleneck: The 314a/314b tradeoff suggests the transition family is missing one state variable: the current absolute level. 314b learned good local innovation scale from transition emission, but once sampling began its prior and decoder evolved only in latent-transition space, so long-run anchoring and mean reversion had no direct state input. The next repair should make current level part of the Markov state rather than reverting to a center/residual split.
last_result_summary: Post-experiment analysis of 314a vs 314b isolates a clean mechanism. Absolute-level emission supplies long-run anchor but suppresses stochastic scale; pure transition emission restores local scale and coverage, but loses level-aware dynamics. The likely missing ingredient is not another objective trick. It is level-aware transition dynamics: transitions should depend on the current level state as well as latent state and history.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 314c: keep transition emission and the healthy latent-state family from 314b, but condition posterior/prior/decoder on the running current-logit level state. In other words, make the state-space law Markov in (current_level, latent_state, history_context). This is the smallest principled repair to restore anchoring and mean reversion without giving back the coverage and daily-change gains.
